# Implementation plan — issue #4701

Planning ref: `main` at `66707437b53aa54446d661c8f409795577d13ead`. The planning context specifies no integration branch, so there is no ref mismatch. The auto-answer maps to the clarifier’s “no questions needed” result; no design choice was supplied as a separate answer.

Scope-mode: Selective Expansion  
Reuse-audit: extends `_has_active_autofix_run`, `_load_actions_runs_cached`, and the merge train’s release snapshot  
Scope-mode justification: Securing dispatches 1–3 without updating the other consumers of head-branch run identity would leave duplicate-dispatch and empty-commit races. Include the consumer wrapper and those directly affected guards, but not the separately tracked post-commit retrigger in #4898. This follows §6’s Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed ordering; the complete safe change is larger than the ≤30-LOC/≤10-minute shortcut threshold.

## Automation integration

- Extend existing scripts and workflows; introduce no standalone script, supervisor, or database operation. No future-removal registry entry is needed.
- Existing entry points remain: `internal-orchestrate-poll.yml` (`*/5` schedule), `cancel_on_pr_close.yml` (PR-close and scheduled release), and `forward-merge-stable-to-main.yml` (`stable` push). No operator invocation or new schedule is required.

## Files likely to change

- `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh` — dispatch ref, PR-named run detection, retrigger, stall-judge, and directly affected empty-commit guards.
- `scripts/review_merge_train.sh` — release dispatch and its existing active-run snapshot.
- `.github/workflows/forward-merge-stable-to-main.yml` — fallback-PR dispatch.
- `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml` — PR-bearing run name for consumer dispatches. Keep the existing name in `.github/workflows/internal-review.yml`.
- `tests/test_conflict_dispatch_active_run_visibility.py`, `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`, `tests/test_review_merge_train.py` — update contrary assertions and add behavioral coverage for each site.
- `agents.md` — correct its statement that forward-merge dispatch uses the fallback head ref.
- `changelog.d/4701-review-dispatch-default-branch.md` — add a `<!-- changelog: security -->` fragment; do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Functions and behavior

1. In `_dispatch_review_for_conflicts` and `_mt_dispatch_review`, validate the PR number as a positive integer and omit `--ref` from review dispatches. Preserve the existing, normalized `allow_workflow_edits` configuration input; pass no PR branch, title, or body as dispatch data. `gh workflow run` without `--ref` selects the remote default-branch workflow, whereas `--ref` selects a branch’s workflow version. ([cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_workflow_run?utm_source=openai))
2. In the forward-merge fallback step, validate the PR number emitted by PR creation/lookup and dispatch `internal-review.yml` without `--ref`. Although the workflow creates the branch itself, its `stable`-derived workflow copy can differ from the protected default-branch copy; branch provenance is not a reason to retain executable-workflow selection by head ref. Keep the fallback PR and nonfatal dispatch-failure behavior.
3. Give dispatched consumer `ai-review.yml` runs an exact `AI Review [pr:<N>]` run name, alongside the existing internal name. Extend the poller’s existing PR-named-run lookup for both names, restricted to `workflow_dispatch` and the appropriate review workflow. Reuse it after head-branch misses rather than introducing per-PR calls in a loop. `gh run list` exposes `--event`, `--limit`, `displayTitle`, `status`, `conclusion`, and `createdAt` for this purpose. ([cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_run_list?utm_source=openai))
4. Make the retrigger lookup consider a matching PR-named run when its branch lookup has no applicable run. Distinguish active runs from completed failures and use the newest applicable result; an older failure must not trigger a dispatch over newer review work. Make the stall judge include matching runs from its existing `_load_actions_runs_cached` snapshot without another API call.
5. Extend the two empty-commit push guards’ cached-run matching to PR-named dispatches. On a cache miss immediately before a push, extend the existing direct in-flight fallback rather than trusting the stale snapshot. Extend the merge train’s **single release snapshot** to key matching dispatched runs by PR as well as legacy branch, including workflow paths carrying an `@ref` suffix. Preserve its claim, label-restoration, and fail-open behavior.

## Data structures and API/interface changes

No new public input, environment variable, or persistent schema. Run-list matching gains an in-memory PR key derived only from an exact review run name and `workflow_dispatch` event; legacy branch keys remain. Document any shared lookup’s input, result, API-call bound, and cache-miss fallback.

The GitHub dispatch API requires a `ref`; the existing CLI supplies the default branch when `--ref` is omitted. Do **not** substitute a raw REST dispatch that omits `ref`. The workflows already declare `workflow_dispatch` inputs. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflows?utm_source=openai))

## Security considerations

The trust boundary is PR metadata entering an Actions-write-capable dispatch whose workflow inherits secrets and has write permissions. Reject missing, zero, nonnumeric, or malformed PR numbers before dispatch; never use a PR head ref to choose executable workflow code. Match run identity using event, workflow, and exact PR-bearing title—not a PR-authored title alone. No new endpoint or authorization grant is proposed; existing GitHub token permissions remain necessary. On lookup or dispatch failure, preserve the current warnings and recovery paths rather than silently treating an unknown run as confirmed absent.

## Risks and edge cases

- **Codebase conflict:** `tests/test_conflict_dispatch_active_run_visibility.py` currently *requires* the forward-merge `--ref`, and `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py` expects a head ref in one dispatch. Update these tests with the code, not around it.
- `workflow-templates/ai-review.yml` currently has no dispatched-run name; consumer installations need their normal wrapper update before its new PR-key matching is effective. Legacy branch matching remains for older runs.
- Bounded run listings and cached snapshots can miss a run. Preserve the existing miss-path direct check where a push could invalidate an editor, and log uncertainty without claiming exhaustive coverage.
- The issue comment reports an implementation in progress on project branch `claude/implement-plan-issue-4701-review-dispatch-default-branch`, with draft PR #4709. That branch was not present in this local planning checkout; reconcile its existing work before implementing or opening another PR. The comment also assigns the review workflow’s post-commit retrigger to #4898, outside this plan.

## Decisions

### D1 — Select the workflow from the default branch
- **Chosen:** Omit `--ref` at all three identified dispatch sites; retain PR number and existing configuration input.
- **Alternatives considered:** Keep the workflow-created forward-merge branch as an exception; pin each dispatch to a separately resolved SHA.
- **Why:** A single default-branch rule removes the executable head-ref boundary without a new lookup or pin-management path.

### D2 — Reuse run identity across recovery paths
- **Chosen:** Extend existing run lookups and snapshots to recognize exact PR-named dispatches while retaining branch-based matching.
- **Alternatives considered:** Add an unconditional per-PR Actions API query to every guard.
- **Why:** Existing snapshots supply the stall judge and merge train; only a relevant miss needs the bounded direct lookup.

## Testing considerations

Update the representative visibility contract in `tests/test_conflict_dispatch_active_run_visibility.py`. Exercise invalid PR numbers and absent `--ref` at each dispatch site; internal and consumer PR names; active `queued`/`pending`/`in_progress` runs; newest-run failure ordering; stall-judge cache matching; empty-commit suppression; merge-train paths with `@ref`; and lookup/dispatch failure recovery. Run focused tests and repository-pinned lint/workflow checks, including the workflow file-size guard. This planning pass ran no validators and changed no files.

## Pre-execution self-check

Files, entry points, trust boundary, compatibility path, and test targets are identified. The existing project work needs reconciliation, but does not prevent implementation from the stated planning ref.
